author: 0xnut6
text: BTCPay Server told operators to shut down at 22:25 UTC Sunday, yet its own servers on v2.4.7 were not touched. Lead developer @NicolasDorier says the swept instances so far look like ones still running versions before 2.4.2.

author: SecAlertsCo
text: Windows Shell command injection was actively exploited in October, while unauthenticated flaws in FortiMail and GitLab opened direct paths to critical systems.

author: toordog
text: PHP2Shell is being actively exploited. Two critical PHP flaws let attackers run code on a server with no login. Fixes only cover PHP 8.2 and newer. Older versions have no real fix: they need an upgrade.

author: Soar_Infosec
text:
If you run Linux servers, a kernel bug called Fragnesia is being actively exploited (CVE-2026-46300).

CISA added it to the KEV list Oct 28 and gave federal agencies until Oct 31. It's being chained with the PHP2Shell bugs to plant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

author: Nulltap_
text:
Google and Mandiant saw an ARTEX agent fire 27 AWS permission events in 23 seconds using stolen credentials.

First check: scope workload credentials down so a stolen identity can reach fewer resources during a burst.

author: Threatpingapp
text: Actively exploited: CVE-2026-111357 in Ivanti Connect Secure (CVSS 7.0). Ivanti Connect Secure Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability.

text:

author: Python_s_
text: Beta9 Sandbox File API Allows Access Outside Tenant Containers. Beam Cloud Beta9 Worker, CVE-2026-120307, CRITICAL (CVSS 9.9). Affected: Worker before 0.1.756 (JFrog CNA disclosure; fix released September 15).

text:

author: cvedotnow
text: Exploited in the wild (CISA KEV): Gitea remote code execution in diffpatch API (CVE-2026-60004). Public exploit, EPSS 0.24. Patch to 1.27.1.

author: Real_Willsec
text: CISA added two actively exploited flaws to KEV. CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 10.0) lets unauthenticated attackers run code on GitLab CE/EE servers via crafted CI/CD configs. Federal agencies were told to patch by Nov 1, today. Via The Hacker News #infosec https://t.co/0eOidbj6s5

author: EmunaEliran
text:
At least nine AI developer platforms disclosed incidents in October, and Wiz traced keys stolen in these breaches to resale sites.

One key drove about 1.7 million AWS Bedrock calls in 13 hours. Rotate keys you stored on them.

https://t.co/jlvAbYMvmq
#AISecurity #LLMJacking https://t.co/zz98WUW9Id

author: foryangxin
text:

author: cveintelligence
text: Critical 9.2, CVE-2026-119050: Agno (through 3.1.11) unsafe reflection in PandasTools. Prompt injection can make the agent call getattr()-resolved pandas functions like read_pickle for code execution or file reads. No patch listed yet.

text:

author: ThreatWire_
text: PoC RELEASED: CVE-2026-112487 (macOS Storage). A path handling flaw lets an app already on a Mac gain root privileges. Public exploit code appeared on 31 Oct. Fixed: Golden Gate 27.2, Tahoe 26.7.2, Sequoia 15.8.2 (26 Oct).

author: CodingNoobie
text: The FBI attributed the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korea's TraderTraitor group; Binance recovered approximately 95% of the stolen funds.

author: Python_s_
text: Stolen Credentials Used for Approximately 2.5 Million Amazon Bedrock API Calls (Wiz Research, Oct 30). Two enterprise credentials linked to an unnamed compromised AI developer-platform vendor.

author: Lhmisme
text: "Ignore all instructions" gets flagged HIGH by Cisco AI Defense's mcp-scanner. "Ignore all previous instructions" comes back SAFE. Tested mcp-scanner 4.8.7, the newest release on PyPI.

text: Drupal Commerce Forceful Browsing (CVE-2026-118539): in-the-wild checkout scraping, session bypass exfiltrates PII, emergency patch released.

author: heygalatea
text:
Last week I said patch PHP.
This week attackers checked.

PHP2Shell and Node2Shell both hit KEV. Five more things need you before Monday, and the versions are inside. https://t.co/Tu3cEUqGeY

author: sunglasses_dev
text: One key left in a public file. Months later it opened a GitHub token, and a poisoned LiteLLM update shipped to PyPI. This is called a supply chain attack. Sunglasses scans files for keys like that and blocks them. Via The Hacker News. https://t.co/SFAwUI6liC

author: Orb44Com
text:
This week the edge and the web stack both got punched in the face again. 

PHP2Shell is still the loudest thing in the room, Ivanti is handing out root on VPN gear, and a low-severity ESXi logging bug is quietly helping people stay invisible.

author: starswarm
text: CISA added 8 actively exploited bugs to its KEV catalog Oct 27-30, in Adobe Commerce/Magento, Google Brotli, GitLab, Cisco ASA/FTD, VMware ESX, the Linux kernel and Ivanti Connect Secure. Run any of them? Patch internet-facing systems first. #CyberSecurity https://t.co/UVUHV6BhXW

author: Lawonxyz
text:
The strangest part of the $200,000 AI wallet exploit? Grok did its job.

It translated Morse code.

The mistake came when Bankrbot treated the translation as an instruction to move money.

Imagine your phone reading a scam SMS aloud, then opening your banking app and paying the https://t.co/HCfqDhMkfZ

author: FixMyVibe
text: VulnCheck flagged 9 MCP servers (Oct 27) that pass tool arguments into a shell: shell=True, exec, execSync. If your MCP tool builds a command from model input, one prompt injection can run commands on your box.

author: FadyEid
text: A ChatGPT share link could read your chats: a crafted share link could run code, read a visitor's chats and send them out. OpenAI paid $5,000 and has not said whether anyone was hit.

author: realNickPawlak
text: On Friday, Chainalysis disclosed that an external attacker got into its systems and internal tools earlier in October. Accessed: user IDs, full names, email addresses...

author: ParallaxBrief
text: The VPN software guarding thousands of corporate and government networks is being actively exploited — again. CISA just added two new Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to its must-patch list, raising a harder question: why does the front door keep failing?

author: lyrie_ai
text: LiteLLM: an admin key was committed to a public repo on May 27, deleted 3 hours later but never revoked. An attacker used it on Oct 10, leading to a poisoned LiteLLM release on PyPI.

author: foukation
text: An infostealer now uses AI to decide which victims are worth targeting. Cisco Talos found a sample called VOLTA that turns stolen credentials, receipts and order history into a profile, then asks an LLM to rank the victim's value.
